test_title: SSC CGL (2022) Tier-II Official Paper (Held On : 3 March 2023)
subject: general
question: The average of 20 numbers is 32. If two numbers are 29 and 31, then what is the average of the remaining numbers (correct up to two decimals)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial average of 20 numbers = 32.

Numbers removed = 29 and 31 (Total = 60).

Deviation from average = (29 − 32) + (31 − 32) = −3 + (−1) = −4.

Since the removed sum (60) is less than the expected sum (32 × 2 = 64), the average will increase.

Net increase in average = 4 ÷ 18 ≈ 0.22.

New average = 32 + 0.22 = 32.22.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n₁) = 20

Initial average (A₁) = 32

Numbers to be removed = 29 and 31

**Formula:** Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e23ddbd157f7b74cefb3fe2f5452474bdfb2ca3a5c4b071e7e959d7b59bc0354.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ Total sum of 20 numbers = 20 × 32 = 640

⇒ Sum of the two removed numbers = 29 + 31 = 60

⇒ Sum of the remaining numbers = 640 − 60 = 580

⇒ Total remaining numbers = 20 − 2 = 18

⇒ Average of remaining numbers = 580 ÷ 18

⇒ Average = 290 ÷ 9 = 32.222...

**∴ The correct answer is 32.22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of First n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Effect of Replacement on Average

When a value x is replaced by y, the New Average = Old Average + (y − x) ÷ Total Count.

Weighted Average

For two groups with averages A₁, A₂ and counts n₁, n₂, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p
